stories.title: Interpreting Autistic Cues Is Difficult, a Teen Built an App That’s Helping Hundreds of Families
stories.summary: Watching adults constantly misread his autistic cousin's cues, New Jersey teen Shashank Madala taught himself machine learning and built Kora — a free app that offers caregivers multiple possible readings of what a child might be feeling. It's now used by 700+ families in 12 countries.
stories.extended_summary: Shashank Madala was 15, with exactly one computer science class behind him, when he decided to fix something he'd watched his whole life: adults guessing wrong about what his autistic cousin was feeling. He taught himself machine learning and built Kora, a free app that offers caregivers several possible interpretations of a child's cues — no scores, no diagnoses, no judgments. Early versions gave one confident answer, but Madala realized that repeated the exact mistake his family made, so he rebuilt it to slow adults down and surface uncertainty. The result: 700+ users across 12 countries, reaching families through autism therapy centers, all free. His philosophy flips the script — technology shouldn't change the child, it should help adults look closer.
